verdict.pair_reasons:
X vs Y — tie, because the verified material differences run in both directions and roughly cancel. X uniquely finds the site the key rates hardest: scripts/ship-land.sh:1739's detached `subprocess.Popen(["bash", sys.argv[1]], …, start_new_session=True)` inside a single-quoted `python3 -c`, with the path resolved at :1730 and handed over at :1741 — I confirmed every line, including the guard at :1731-1733, the kill switch at :1727 and X's correct reading that `2>/dev/null || true` suppresses only python3's own failure. X also answers brief part (b) at roughly ten times Y's coverage (~120 adjudicated near-misses vs 15); I sampled 20 of X's and every one is a real line, correctly classified. Against that, Y finds two in-scope sites X misses, both of them the "generic dispatcher handed the path at runtime" case the brief explicitly named: bin/cc-premise:1392 (`["/bin/sh","-c",cmd]` on a falsifier deploy-live.sh mints at :960 and files at :1046/:1261) and bin/cc-do:454 (`bash -c "$cmd"` on a `needs --run` row deploy-live.sh files at :811-812 with commands built at :708/:734/:746). Consequently X states two wrong headline answers — "Total … 5" asserted as exhaustive, and (c)'s claim that the only unattended entry point is outside the scoped trees, which I refuted directly (launchd com.chrisren.autonomy-sweep → scripts/autonomy-sweep.sh:1488 → bin/cc-premise sweep → :1392) — while Y asserts nothing false and names scripts/ship-land.sh in its own unread list. Y adds five verified stale-citation findings the brief's closing paragraph asks for. Neither side's advantage dominates.

X vs Z — Z. Z has the same two-site census advantage as Y (cc-premise:1392 and cc-do:454, both verified), and unlike X it gets brief question (c) right in substance: it states that the only scheduled path performing a real advance is the out-of-scope plist while an in-scope unattended executor also exists via claim/sweep, which is the key's N4 correction that X flatly contradicts. Z also lands a material finding neither X nor the key has, and I traced it end to end: --offline forces DRY_RUN=1 at deploy-live.sh:429, yet `link_refresh` is called unconditionally at :1952 ahead of the --offline block at :1959, runs deploy-parity-assert at :1483, and calls copy_drift_notice at :1493 which writes $PAGES_DIR/deploy-copy-drift.page at :1422 with no DRY_RUN check — so the "read-only probe" at operator-readout.sh:534 and cc-do:184 can write. X's near-miss list is far richer and its ship-land trace is excellent, but that does not offset a definitively-wrong site total plus a wrong answer to an explicitly-asked question.

Y vs Z — Z. Same six sites, same disclosed ship-land gap, same zero wrong claims, so the split is on verified extras. Z alone has the dry-run-is-not-write-free finding above. Z's answer to (c) is the stronger one: Y offers the in-scope unattended path only as "one unverified possibility", whereas Z names both in-scope unattended modes and cites the exact comments (bin/cc-premise:9-11, :431-437) that are its only evidence. Z read cc-premise's run_falsifier region including the definition and adds the --falsify-host exit contract (:405-408, :406, :339-340, :372-375) and the fact that cc-backlog only stores a falsifier and never runs it at filing (:1898, :2221-2227, :2273-2285) — all of which I verified — where Y had to caveat that it never saw the function header. Y's one clear edge is a fifth stale citation (deploy-live.sh:1679's ":540" vs the real :660) and a slightly longer stale-citation audit; that is smaller than Z's set of verified extras.
